messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: qplot - Changing Size of Circles in Proportion Plot
parts:
What's your size aesthetic?? I don't see one in your code. (BTW, you
might want to look at scale_area() rather than scale_size() if you
want to maintain proportionality.)

Your purpose is not clear to me: from your post, I learned that you're
plotting proportions, are using stat_sum() and want to increase the
size of the circles. Why are you using stat_sum()? By what criterion
do you want to "increase the size of the circles"? I think you'd get a
better targeted response by providing a reproducible example with a
more explicit statement of purpose.

Dennis

On Mon, Mar 11, 2013 at 2:03 PM, Jeff Bruce <jeff...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi all,
>
> I have this data set and I'm plotting proportions using qplot and stat_sum()
> with the following command:
>
> qplot(stim_deg, resp_deg, data=locdata, stat="sum", group=stim_deg,
> scale_size(c(1,10)))
>
> One problem I'm having is I want to increase the size of the circles in the
> plot. I've tried using the size parameter, but that just overrides the
> proportion values, and I've also tried scale_size_continuous() to no avail.
> cex is only available in plot(), so what am I to use for ggplot2?
>
> Cheers

messages.subject: Re: qplot - Changing Size of Circles in Proportion Plot
parts:
Thanks for your reply Dennis.  I apologize, I'm new to this package.  I'll provide more details.

Here's an example data frame:

stim_deg   resp_deg
0                0  
0                0
0                0 
1                0
1                1
1                2
.                 .
.                 .
.                 .
6                4
6                4
6                5

I'm aiming to produce a plot which shows stim_deg on the x axis and resp_deg on the y axis, with circle size representing the proportion of responses for that (stim_deg, resp_deg) configuration.   So for example, the circle at (0,0) should have proportion = 1, because there are no responses at stim_deg = 0 other than resp_deg = 0.  The circle at (1,0) should have proportion = 0.33, because there exist resp_deg = 0,1,2 at stim_deg = 1.  I've managed to produce this plot with my qplot command, but the circles are too small.  How do I increase the size of the circles?

command to produce the plot:
qplot(stim_deg, resp_deg, data=locdata, stat="sum", group=stim_deg)

Cheers

messages.author: de0353bdfec15530
messages.subject: Re: qplot - Changing Size of Circles in Proportion Plot
parts:
For anyone who is interested, I resolved the issue.

The answer was to create a ggplot, then add scale_size_continuous(to = c(1,15)).
